proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XII currently runs only one way: Licensee indemnifies Licensor for essentially all use of the licensed technology, and Article XIII expressly excludes Licensor liability for infringement claims. We have added a Licensor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breaches it causes and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct (with standard notice/control/cooperation and remedies), and narrowed our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of law, consistent with our playbook position. If helpful, we can accept the customary infringement exclusions (Licensee modifications, combinations and specifications) and a super-cap at 3x annual fees.

Failure to give prompt notice shall relieve the indemnifying party of its obligations only to the extent it is materially prejudiced thereby.

proposal.summary: Add Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity to Article XII and narrow the one-way Licensee indemnity

quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all suits, claims, proceedings, judgments, awards, damages, loss, liability, cost and expenses
rationale: Article XII is a one-way indemnity running only from Licensee to Licensor, drafted extremely broadly (Licensee's exercise of the licence, the conduct of Licensee's business, and any breach of any term). There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the agreement, and Article XIII goes further by expressly excluding any Licensor liability for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party intellectual property rights. That is squarely walk-away territory under this rule (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity) and fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Our redline inserts a Licensor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Licensor-caused data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and reciprocal notice-control-cooperation mechanics (expressly overriding Article XIII so the indemnity is not gutted), and narrows our own indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law. The fallback (customary infringement exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology and all Derivative Works but says nothing about our data or about the customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), leaving us with no ownership and no surviving licence. We have added a carve-out confirming we retain our trading and client data, that paid-for deliverables are assigned to us subject to Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP (licensed back to us on a perpetual, royalty-free basis), and that no joint ownership is created; if Licensor prefers, we can instead take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense those deliverables.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (i) Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data and content submitted by or on behalf of Licensee to, or generated by Licensee's use of, the Licensed Technology, including Licensee's trading, order, position, client and account data ("Licensee Data"), and nothing in this Agreement transfers or assigns to Licensor any ownership of Licensee Data or of any other intellectual property of Licensee; (ii) all customization work, client front ends, deliverables and other work product developed by Licensor specifically for Licensee and paid for by Licensee (including pursuant to Article VII(b)) (the "Licensee Deliverables") shall be owned by Licensee, and Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest therein, excluding Licensor's pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights and the underlying Licensed Technology, which Licensor retains and in respect of which Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense such retained materials solely as embedded in the Licensee Deliverables; and (iii) nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee ownership of its data and of paid-for customization deliverables, with a licence-back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership.

quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
rationale: Article III is a one-way ownership clause: Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) is defined solely as rights "of Licensor". "Derivative Work" (1.3) sweeps in "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology", so the bespoke customization and unique client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in Licensor. There is no assignment to us and no licence back beyond the limited, non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence, which terminates on expiry with an obligation to return everything (Article XXI). The Agreement is also silent on our data: Confidential Information (1.2) protects only information disclosed to Licensee, and nothing confirms we retain our trading, order, client and account data. Vendor keeping its platform is fine, but the clause fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) and leaves Customer Data ownership unaddressed. We added a narrow carve-out: we retain our data and IP; paid-for deliverables are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP and granting a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials; and no joint ownership is created.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need the liability cap to be mutual and at a meaningful level: today only Licensor is capped (at one half of amounts paid) while our liability is unlimited, which is outside our playbook. We have set a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap, and fees payable not treated as capped damages.

ops.newText: (b) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. THE EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS IN SUBSECTION (a) SHALL NOT APPLY TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, AND LICENSEE'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS CAP.
ops.oldText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.

proposal.summary: Make the Article XIII cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 and add standard uncapped carve-outs

quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
rationale: Article XIII is one-sided and sits in walk-away territory. The cap in (b) protects only Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid — far below even 6 months' fees — while Licensee's liability is entirely uncapped and is in fact expanded by the broad Article XII indemnity (p0128–p0129). The exclusion of indirect/consequential damages in (a) also runs only in Licensor's favour and expressly excludes all IP infringement liability. There are no carve-outs at all for confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, so the clause fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct). Redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, adds the standard uncapped Excluded Claims, disapplies (a) to those claims, and confirms Licensee's fee obligations are not capped "damages".
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need to be able to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and a change of control of Licensee cannot automatically terminate the Agreement or our licenses — our playbook treats a blanket assignment bar and a change-of-control termination right as walk-away items. We have made the consent standard mutual and reasonable, and kept Licensor from assigning to a competitor of ours; if helpful, we can instead move to mutual assignment to successors on written notice.

ops.newText: Licensee may assign this Agreement and its rights hereunder, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. Otherwise, neither party may assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its rights hereunder in whole or in part without the other party's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned; provided that Licensor shall not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Licensee.
ops.oldText: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.

ops.newText: (a) A Change of Control (as defined below) of Licensee shall not terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder, and shall not give rise to any right of Licensor to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement; provided that Licensee shall give Licensor written notice of any Change of Control within thirty (30) days after its consummation.
ops.oldText: (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control. For purposes of the preceding sentence, Licensor will be deemed to have reasonably withheld its consent to a Change of Control if any person or entity who would acquire direct or indirect control (as defined below) of Licensee pursuant to such Change of Control then conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive with a business then conducted by Licensor or any of its Affiliates and/or Licensor reasonably believes that Licensor's interests will be adversely effected by the continuing of this Agreement upon such a Change in Control.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee affiliate/successor assignment carve-out with mutual reasonable-consent standard, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.

quote: (c) ASSIGNMENT. Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
rationale: Two walk-away features. First, Section (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149) imposes a blanket bar on any Licensee assignment or transfer without Licensor's prior written consent, with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and imposes no reciprocal restriction on Licensor (so Licensor may freely assign, including to our competitors). Second, Article XX (p0134) provides that on any Change of Control of Licensee — defined in p0135 to include a sale of substantially all assets, merger or majority equity transfer — this Agreement and all Licensee's licenses "shall automatically terminate" absent Licensor's advance written consent, and Licensor is deemed reasonable in refusing consent if it merely believes its interests would be adversely affected. That is worse than a Vendor termination right on our change of control; combined with the Article XXII right of first refusal over our M&A transactions (p0139), it materially impedes our corporate transactions. This fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Licensee, makes the residual consent requirement mutual and not unreasonably withheld, bars Licensor assignment to our competitors, and replaces automatic change-of-control termination with a notice obligation. Fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice) is offered in the comment. The Article XXII ROFR is noted but not separately redlined here.

quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth belo
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us. Every exclusivity reference runs the other way or is neutral: the licence is expressly "Non Exclusive" (Preamble, p0030, p0049, p0052), and Licensor retains the right to license the technology to others (p0043) — i.e. no exclusivity is granted to us and none is demanded of us. There is no requirements commitment, no covenant not to procure FX technology or services from third parties, and no obligation to route volume solely through the Platform (searches for "sole"/"exclusive"/"third party"/"all transactions" return nothing of that kind). The defined term flagged in the planner hint, "Right of First Refusal" (Article XXII, p0139), is a change-of-control/exit right — a 5-business-day right to match a third-party offer to buy Licensee's assets or merge with Licensee — not a restriction on sourcing alternative suppliers, and it expressly releases us to close with the third party if not exercised (p0140–p0141). The restrictions in Article II (e.g. p0027, p0041, p0044) are ordinary licence-scope and anti-sublicensing limits on use of Licensor's own technology, not exclusive-dealing covenants. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer); no redline required. Noted for the record only: the ROFR and the Change of Control provision (p0134) constrain our exit flexibility and are separately reviewable under assignment/change-of-control rules, not under this rule.

quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, DAMAGES FOR THE LOSS OF GOODWILL, PROSPECTIVE PROFITS OR ANTICIPATED INCOME, OR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM ANY EXPENDITURES, INVESTMENTS, LEASES OR COMMITMENTS MADE BY EITHER PARTY ON ACCOUNT OF THE TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION OF THIS AGREEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS TERMS.
rationale: The agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination fee or minimum/accelerated fee on the Licensee, so it meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). The payment provisions (Articles V and the fee schedule, p0050–p0074, p0086) are usage-based license, support and supplemental payments only, with no shortfall charge or penalty interest. Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages for both parties, and Article XXI (p0138) requires only return of the Licensed Technology on termination. Article IV (p0049) preserves the Licensor's right to "receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" after termination, which is payment for services actually used rather than a liquidated sum, and the audit cost-shift in p0064 (triggered only by a discrepancy over 5%) is a cost-reimbursement mechanic, not a penalty. Noted only for the record: there is no service-credit or vendor-side remedy running to us, but that is outside this rule.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

As a fallback we can accept Affiliate use on written notice to Licensor.

quote: iii. Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
rationale: The grant in p0030 runs to Licensee alone, and p0045 (read with p0041/p0042 and Article VI at p0085) bars access by anyone other than Licensee's own employees, so Affiliates and contractors acting for us are excluded with only a discretionary Licensor-consent path — short of even the fallback (Affiliates covered on written notice). Transferability also fails the fallback: p0149 bars assignment without Licensor's consent with no successor/M&A carve-out, and Article XX (p0134) auto-terminates the licence on a Change of Control absent consent, which Licensor is deemed reasonable to withhold whenever it "reasonably believes" its interests are adversely affected. We therefore propose the minimal preferred edits: extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, conform the employee-only restriction, and add a consent-free successor transfer right; Affiliate use on written notice remains an acceptable fallback. The licence is not revocable at will on its face (36-month initial term), so we have not addressed the no-cure termination right in Article IV under this rule.

quote: Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on our other businesses, so the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer) is met. The only Licensee-side restrictions are ordinary license-scope limits on use of the Licensor's own Licensed Technology (the "Field of Use" definition in 1.5 and the Additional Restrictions in Article II, including no sublicensing, no reverse engineering and no Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology); none of these prevents us from trading on, buying or building competing FX platforms, or from operating any line of business. Article X is a non-solicitation of Licensor employees only (no non-compete), and the license is expressly non-exclusive with no minimum-volume or exclusive-routing commitment. Noted but not flagged here: the change-of-control consent in Article XX (p0134) lets Licensor deem consent reasonably withheld where an acquirer competes with Licensor, which is an assignment/change-of-control point rather than a restrictive covenant on our operations and is addressed under the assignment rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a refund of prepaid fees, because the Agreement locks us into a 36-month term with no exit other than for cause; our playbook does not accept a multi-year commitment without a convenience right. We can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: IV Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty, early termination charge or further liability for fees accruing after the effective date of termination, in which case Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of such termination. Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension or renewal thereof.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term.

quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period"). The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
rationale: The Agreement commits Licensee to a 36-month Initial Period (renewable at Licensor's option) and the only termination rights anywhere in the document are for cause or upon defined events: Licensor's immediate termination for any Licensee breach (Art. IV, Art. II/p0043), mutual insolvency termination (Art. XIX), automatic termination on a Licensee Change of Control and Licensor termination on Licensee wind-up (Art. XX), with Art. XXI/XXIII addressing only the effects of termination. There is no Licensee right to terminate for convenience on any notice period, which falls below both the preferred (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and fallback (60-90 days' notice, fee capped at 3 months) positions and is walk-away territory for a multi-year term. On the other side, Licensor has no convenience right, which is consistent with the playbook, so our redline only adds the Licensee exit and confirms the position for Licensor.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have capped these record audits at once per twelve months, during normal business hours and on 30 days' prior written notice, and required the auditor to be bound by confidentiality, consistent with our policy against open-ended audit rights. The 5% cost-shift threshold and the records-only scope are unchanged.

ops.newText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor, provided that (i) no more than one (1) such audit may be conducted in any twelve (12) month period, (ii) Licensor shall give Licensee not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice of the audit, (iii) the audit shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Licensee's operations, and (iv) the auditor shall be bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.

proposal.summary: Cap audits at once per 12 months, during business hours, on 30 days' notice, with the auditor bound by confidentiality.

quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
rationale: The audit right binding us (Licensee) sits in Article II.IV(b) (p0073), with cost allocation at p0064. Several elements already meet the preferred position: the auditor must be an independent CPA/audit professional selected by mutual agreement, the scope is limited to accounting records (no access to our systems), we get a 30-day lead time from Licensor's written request, and Licensor bears the cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found. However, there is no frequency limit at all, so Licensor could demand audits repeatedly — unlimited audits fall in walk-away territory under this rule and fail the fallback's "once per year" requirement. The clause is also silent on business hours and on binding the auditor to confidentiality. We therefore proposed the minimal insert capping audits at one per twelve months, on 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, with the auditor bound by confidentiality; the 5% cost-shift threshold and records-only scope are left untouched.

quote: shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A., applicable to contracts entered in and performed entirely within the State of New York, U.S.A. without regard to any conflict of law principles.
rationale: The Agreement is governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, and disputes must be brought in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the SDNY or the New York state courts, plus waivers of venue objections and forum non conveniens. That matches the preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York courts). A search of the document returns no arbitration provision, so there is no foreign-seated arbitration risk. The only immaterial variance is that venue is framed as the City of New York rather than New York County specifically, which is noted but not redlined.

quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
rationale: The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation of any kind. Fees are set by a fixed tiered per-US$1m schedule (p0056–p0063) with no requirement that Licensee offer Licensor rates or terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and no obligation to match third-party offers; the fee, supplemental payment (p0078), support (p0086–p0089) and general provisions sections are all silent on comparison to other counterparties. The only third-party-comparison mechanic is Licensor's Right of First Refusal over a sale or merger of Licensee (p0139), which is a change-of-control right rather than an MFN on commercial terms and is addressed under the assignment/change-of-control rules, not here. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer). We note the flip side — Licensor grants us no MFN pricing either — but that is an upside ask, not a deviation, so no redline is proposed.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
rationale: The fee architecture is purely usage-based and meets the preferred position: user fees are a tiered rate "per US$1million traded (for each one-way part of the trade)" applied to actual Monthly Notional Volume (p0056–p0058, p0070). A full-text review found no minimum purchase commitment, no committed volume, no take-or-pay, no shortfall or make-whole payment, and no volume cap on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shall be no less than" and "per month" return nothing of that character. The only fixed amounts are the already-advanced $35,000 initial payment (p0051) and $2,500 per month for Technical Support Services (p0086), which are fees for ordered services rather than a purchase commitment. The volume tiers operate only to reduce the per-million rate as volume rises, so higher volume benefits us. The "In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded ... as being traded" language in p0070 is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a committed minimum. Noted for context only (not a deviation under this rule): the initial term is 36 months and renewal is at Licensor's option (p0049) — term/renewal control is addressed under the term and termination rules, not as a take-or-pay exposure, since no spend is committed over that term. No redline proposed.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the non-solicit mutual and narrowed it to personnel directly involved in this Agreement for 12 months from the end of their involvement, consistent with our playbook position on restrictive covenants; a three-year restriction covering every Licensor and Affiliate employee is far broader than the engagement. The existing general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-out is retained.

ops.newText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the twelve (12) month period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who was directly involved in the performance or receipt of this Agreement to leave his or her employment with such other party; provided that this restriction shall in no event apply to any such person more than twelve (12) months after the end of that person's involvement.
ops.oldText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.

proposal.summary: Make non-solicit mutual, limit to personnel involved in the Agreement, and reduce duration from three years to 12 months.

quote: (b) NON SOLICITATION. During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.
rationale: Article X(b) binds only us (Licensee) and runs for the Term plus three years post-termination, covering any person employed by Licensor or its Affiliates rather than only personnel involved in the engagement. A restriction longer than 24 months that covers all Licensor personnel is walk-away territory under the rule, so the clause fails the fallback on duration, scope and mutuality. On the positive side, "Solicit" is defined narrowly and already carves out general job advertising and voluntary/unsolicited inquiries, and there is no "no-hire" element, so only duration, scope and mutuality need fixing. Per the redline guidance we narrowed to the fallback (mutual, personnel directly involved, 12 months from the end of involvement) rather than deleting the covenant, retaining the existing carve-out sentence. Note the injunctive-relief clause (p0126) gives Licensor equitable relief for non-solicitation breaches, which magnifies the over-broad scope.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable at the Licensor's sole option; our playbook allows renewal only by mutual written agreement, or 12-month renewals we can decline on 30 days' notice with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. This aligns the renewal sentence with Articles IV.II and IV.III, which already require mutual written agreement; we can discuss a 60-day notice window and a 5% cap if helpful.

ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, provided that either party may elect not to renew by written notice given at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out and capped uplift

quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
rationale: Article IV (p0049) is the only renewal provision in the Agreement. It permits a seven-year extension of the 36-month Initial Period exercisable unilaterally "at the option of the Licensor," with no notice window for us and no cap on renewal pricing. A multi-year renewal we cannot exit is walk-away territory under the rule, and it fails the fallback (auto-renewal with a non-renewal window of ≤60 days and uplift ≤5%) on two material terms: renewal term length and our ability to decline. The clause also conflicts with Articles IV.II and IV.III of the same paragraph, which contemplate extension only "by mutual written" agreement of the parties, so the redline conforms the renewal sentence to the mutual-agreement mechanic already in the document and adds 12-month renewal terms, a 30-day opt-out and a CPI/3% uplift cap (fallback of 60 days and 5% offered in the comment).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property; it gives us no exit path and no right to recover our own trade and account data held on the Licensed Technology. We have added a reciprocal provision giving up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback provided the 30-day data return stays.

ops.text: Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee data, trade, order and account records and other Licensee information in Licensor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data, records and information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Licensee.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligation into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)

quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
rationale: The Agreement contains no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is entirely one-directional: the licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days with officer certification, while "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." Nothing obliges Licensor to help us migrate or to return our own data. Article X confidentiality (p0124) binds only Licensee and has no return/destruction mechanic that could serve, and the other termination articles (XIX insolvency p0132-33, XX change of control p0134-37, XXIII p0142) are silent. This matters because the Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0021, p0033), so our order, trade and account records sit on Licensor's systems; on termination we would have no contractual right to recover them, which sits at or near the walk-away position (no data return). We therefore insert the preferred position at p0138 as a new subsection (c): up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days of assistance with the 30-day export remains available as a fallback.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Licensed Technology is currently provided wholly "AS IS" with every warranty disclaimed, so we have no contractual recourse if the platform fails to work as documented. We have added a standard express warranty (workmanlike services, twelve-month conformance to Documentation, no malicious code, compliance with law) with a repair, replace or refund remedy, and carved it out of the disclaimer; we can accept a ninety (90) day conformance period if a shorter window is needed.

ops.text: Licensor warrants that (a) the Technical Support Services and any other services provided hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following the Acceptance Date, the Licensed Technology will conform in all material respects to its Documentation and Specifications; (c) the Licensed Technology will not contain any virus, worm, disabling device or other malicious code; and (d) Licensor will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. Licensee's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties is, at Licensor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming services or Licensed Technology, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or Licensed Technology.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE, THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS
ops.oldText: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS

proposal.summary: Insert an express performance warranty (12 months software conformance / workmanlike services, no malicious code, legal compliance) with repair-replace-refund remedy, and carve it out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.

quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
rationale: The Agreement contains no express performance warranty anywhere. Article VII obliges Licensor only to use "commercially reasonable efforts to provide Error Corrections" (p0093) and to make Revisions available (p0094), which is a support covenant rather than a warranty, and Article VIX provides the Licensed Technology wholly "AS IS" with all warranties express and implied disclaimed, including any warranty that the technology is error-free, will meet Licensee's requirements, or that nonconformity to its Documentation can or will be corrected (p0110-p0116). That is the playbook's walk-away position: full "AS IS" with no conformance warranty and no remedy, so it fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund). Redline inserts the preferred express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance to Documentation, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair/replace/refund remedy and carves it out of the disclaimer; the fallback 90-day period is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance covenant even though Licensor hosts the platform and handles our trading data and Confidential Information, so we have added our standard requirement (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request). If limits are an issue, we can accept E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber of USD 2,000,000 as a fallback.

ops.text: (l) INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than US$1,000,000 per occurrence and US$2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than US$2,000,000; (iii) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than US$5,000,000, covering Licensor's processing, storage or transmission of Licensee's data and Confidential Information; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Licensor shall provide Licensee with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance provision in General Provisions

quote: (k) REPRESENTATION BY COUNSEL. Each party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to be represented by separate independent counsel in the negotiation of this Agreement
rationale: No insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement: the only occurrence of "insurance" is p0051, which merely makes Licensee responsible for taxes, duties and insurance charges on payments, and the GENERAL PROVISIONS section (p0144-p0159) runs from Governing Law through Representation by Counsel with no insurance sub-clause. Licensor supplies and supports the E-Path FX platform and receives Licensee's data and Confidential Information, so the playbook expects standard vendor coverage; absence of any coverage for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory. Inserted the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new sub-clause (l) after p0159, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged in the comment.
